status: Investigation only; no dependency or production change
baseline_tests: Three Linux x86_64 fixtures passed: dot entries and bulk/cursor order, first-NUL truncation, immediate path errors, rename isolation and thread transfer.
current_path: osd/file/native_unix/directory_cursor.rs owns DIR, calls readdir for every next_name, copies each name once and closes the stream once. A null read returns None but does not prevent a later read.

candidates.name: std::fs::ReadDir
candidates.assessment: Not a direct replacement: filters dot entries that current callers can observe. Synthesizing them does not establish preservation of native ordering.

candidates.name: rustix 1.1.5 Dir
candidates.assessment: The default Linux backend retries interrupted reads. Both backends retain an any_errors flag that prevents subsequent reads after an error. The libc backend can avoid the Linux retry change via use-libc, but still fuses after errors. Entries own a CString; copying into the existing Vec return type adds a name allocation relative to the current path. Costs are not measured yet.
candidates.recovery_limit: seek clears the error flag, but preserving position requires a valid cookie. The libc DirEntry::offset API is not available on macOS; no portable retry-preserving adapter has been demonstrated.

candidates.name: rustix 1.1.5 RawDir
candidates.assessment: Borrows a caller-owned mutable buffer, exposes borrowed names, and calls getdents_uninit without a retry loop in RawDir::next. Reconstructing it for each next_name would discard unread buffered entries. A safe owned-cursor design and supported-target coverage remain unproven; this is not a reason to hide a self-reference cast in a helper.

candidates.name: nix 0.31.3 Dir/OwningIter
candidates.assessment: OwningIter does not fuse read errors, but Dir::from_fd leaks the consumed descriptor on fdopendir failure. The isolated safe probe reproduced ENOTDIR with the descriptor still open twice under Rust 1.99.0. Tracked as Bug #126; nix was not added to Martensite. Entry owns a CString, so allocation costs also need measurement.
candidates.older_version_check: The local 0.29.0 source closes on constructor failure but uses the older readdir_r representation; upstream v0.30.1 has the consumed-descriptor leak. No older version was adopted.

next_requirements: Prove safe ownership and repeated-read behavior, including injected transient read failure
Verify failure cleanup without a shim that assumes ownership of a raw descriptor after a supposedly consuming API
Measure per-entry allocations, elapsed time and peak memory before adoption
Run native fixtures on all affected supported targets
scope_limit: No impossibility or permanent system exception is established. The existing unsafe cursor remains temporary migration work.
